scope: Actual PostgreSQL 17.11 and Garage 2.4.1 on one isolated host using the unchanged deterministic synthetic execution adapter, an independent API and workers, signed development-mode admission, real S3 artifacts, process restarts, abrupt worker lease recovery, two-worker dispatch, quiesced pg_dump/pg_restore and S3 archive recovery into fresh destinations with recovery-lock. Does not qualify real model competence, effectful tools, HA/failover, power-loss durability, a live Kubernetes/Compose deployment, production network isolation or hardware attestation.

network.tls: Loopback development fixture only; no remote TLS qualification

official_binary_provenance.verified_against: official HTTPS release download; observed digest

checks.name: state-engine-connectivity
checks.detail: PostgreSQL accepts SCRAM authentication; Garage created the private default bucket with the supplied official single-node flags.
checks.postgres: PostgreSQL 17.11 (Ubuntu 17.11-1.pgdg24.04+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, 64-bit

checks.name: qualified-process-installation
checks.detail: Independent API and worker use the actual PostgreSQL schema and Garage artifacts; signed qualification has an explicit development-only bootstrap scope.

checks.name: private-result-and-bounded-receipt
checks.detail: Actual independent worker completed a task; private API and S3 bytes agree with the stored SHA-256; caller sees exactly receipt/status; anonymous S3 and caller artifact access are denied.

checks.name: api-worker-restart
checks.detail: Stopped and restarted independent API and worker; completed task, idempotency, private object digest, qualification and receipt survived without replay.

checks.name: postgres-lease-recovery
checks.detail: Abruptly killed only the fixture worker while its task was running. A new process reclaimed the expired PostgreSQL lease and safely reran the explicitly synthetic task; exactly one result was released.

checks.name: postgres-concurrent-workers
checks.detail: Two independent worker processes completed four queued tasks with one attempt per task. Both acquired work and the shared serialized audit chain verifies.

checks.name: quiesced-state-backup
checks.detail: Stopped both workers, retained a deliberately queued recovery fixture, stopped the API, then ran actual pg_dump in custom format and the shipped state_archive.py dump command.

checks.name: state-engine-restart
checks.detail: Gracefully stopped and restarted PostgreSQL and Garage themselves. All rows, the audit head, queued state and every recorded artifact digest survived.

checks.name: fresh-database-and-bucket-restore
checks.detail: Restored the actual PostgreSQL custom-format dump into a separate fresh database and used the shipped archive script to restore six objects into a separate fresh Garage bucket. Table counts, task states, audit head and all referenced object digests match the quiesced source.

checks.name: restored-authority-lock
checks.detail: Applied the real recovery-lock CLI before exposing restored state. Both grants are inhibited; the queued task is blocked without execution; the audit chain extends correctly. Changed database/bucket placement invalidates the old qualification; caller receipts are unavailable while private operator reads still verify.

checks.name: signed-development-state-evidence
checks.detail: Issued an Ed25519 qualification containing the actual successful state-integration checks and explicit development-only limitations, then verified its signature against configured public trust. It binds the original database/bucket placement and fixture generation.

checks.name: isolated-runtime-cleanup
checks.detail: Stopped every task-owned API, worker and state-engine process; all five owned loopback ports are closed. State-engine processes ran as nobody. Fixture credentials, signing key and backups remain private and are excluded from deliverables.

limitations: This is a single-node process installation with actual state engines; Docker Compose and Kubernetes reconciliation were not exercised in this integration.
Graceful database/object-store restart and logical restore were verified; storage power loss, hardware durability, replication, HA, failover and prolonged load were not tested.
Two workers and four concurrent tasks exercise real PostgreSQL locking at a bounded scale; they do not establish throughput or saturation limits.
The synthetic adapter makes lease replay safe by construction. Effectful tools and native request-ledger restore are outside this state-adapter fixture.
The S3 archive script was exercised for a dedicated private bucket while API and workers were quiesced. Backups remain private because database rows and objects contain task payloads.
The signature verifies declared runtime placement and collected evidence. It is not hardware attestation or independent production deployment certification.
Audit continuity was verified against the stored head; full-history replacement still requires external checkpoints to detect.
